clue_en: Great white shark — Which head organs give great white sharks electroreception?
explanation_en: The pits provide one of the shark’s five hunting senses, alongside sight, hearing, smell, and water-flow detection.

clue_en: Chondrichthyes — What toothlike structures cover the skin of cartilaginous fishes?
explanation_en: Dermal denticles protect the skin and streamline water flow over the body.

clue_en: Fujita scale — Tetsuya Fujita developed a scale for which weather phenomenon?
explanation_en: Fujita devised the scale specifically to compare the intensity of tornadoes.

clue_en: Space Shuttle Columbia disaster — Which space shuttle broke apart during re-entry on 1 February 2003?
explanation_en: Columbia became the second Space Shuttle lost in a fatal accident.

clue_en: Great white shark — What is the great white shark’s scientific name?
explanation_en: It is the only living species in Carcharodon.

clue_en: Chondrichthyes — Do most sharks have covered gills or separate gill slits?
explanation_en: Unlike bony fishes, they generally lack a bony operculum.

clue_en: Centipede — What modified appendages deliver centipede venom?
explanation_en: The first trunk appendages form venom claws.

clue_en: Chandra X-ray Observatory — Which high-energy band spans Chandra’s stated observing range of about 0.12 to 12 nanometres?
explanation_en: That wavelength interval corresponds to photon energies of roughly 0.1 to 10 keV.

clue_en: Great white shark — Do great white sharks lay external eggs or bear live young?
explanation_en: Embryos hatch inside the mother before birth.

clue_en: Chondrichthyes — What two major living groups divide Chondrichthyes?
explanation_en: Sharks and rays are elasmobranchs; chimaeras are holocephalans.

clue_en: Centipede — To which arthropod class do centipedes belong?
explanation_en: Chilopods are distinct from millipede class Diplopoda.

clue_en: Shrimp — What abdominal appendages help shrimp swim forward?
explanation_en: Shrimp use pleopods, also called swimmerets, for ordinary forward swimming.

clue_en: Great white shark — What kind of bite may a great white use while investigating an unfamiliar object?
accepted_variants_en: investigatory bite|exploratory bite|bump and bite|test bite
explanation_en: Great whites may investigate unfamiliar objects with a brief test bite rather than a sustained predatory bite.

clue_en: Chondrichthyes — What material chiefly forms a chondrichthyan skeleton?
explanation_en: The class name means cartilage fish.

clue_en: Centipede — How many leg pairs occur on each leg-bearing trunk segment?
explanation_en: Because each leg-bearing segment carries one pair and the segment count is odd, the total cannot be exactly 100.

clue_en: Shrimp — Which structures form the fan at a shrimp’s tail?
explanation_en: The uropods flank the telson to form the tail fan.

clue_en: Western lowland gorilla — What is the western lowland gorilla’s scientific trinomial?
explanation_en: The repeated name marks genus, species, and subspecies.

clue_en: Chondrichthyes — Which animal belongs to class Chondrichthyes: great white shark or tuna?
explanation_en: Sharks are cartilaginous fishes; tuna are bony fishes.

clue_en: Centipede — How many legs can no centipede have exactly?
explanation_en: Odd counts of leg-bearing trunk segments prevent the total from being exactly 100.

clue_en: Shrimp — Common true shrimp such as Palaemon belong to which infraorder?
explanation_en: Carideans are decapods whose second abdominal segment overlaps both the first and third.

clue_en: Western lowland gorilla — Is the western lowland gorilla a species or subspecies?
explanation_en: The third word of its trinomial identifies a taxonomic level below species.

clue_en: Ming (clam) — Why was the clam nicknamed Ming?
response_en: it was born during China’s Ming dynasty
explanation_en: Its estimated birth around 1499 fell within that dynasty.

clue_en: Centipede — What sensory appendages project from a centipede’s head?
explanation_en: The paired antennae carry sensory receptors used to explore the centipede’s surroundings.

clue_en: Shrimp — Which organs do shrimp use for gas exchange?
explanation_en: Water passes over gills beneath the carapace.

clue_en: Western lowland gorilla — What locomotor style uses the middle finger bones to support weight?
explanation_en: Gorillas move quadrupedally on their knuckles.

clue_en: Ming (clam) — In what year was the clam collected near Iceland?
explanation_en: The 2006 collection preceded the revised 2013 age estimate by seven years.

clue_en: Strawberry — Which flower part enlarges into most of the red flesh?
explanation_en: The ovaries remain as surface achenes.

clue_en: Shrimp — Can shrimp propel themselves rapidly backward?
explanation_en: Shrimp can flex the abdomen and tail to move rapidly backward.

clue_en: Western lowland gorilla — Is the western lowland gorilla’s diet mainly plant material or meat?
explanation_en: Fruit, leaves, and stems dominate, with some invertebrates.

clue_en: Ming (clam) — What shell feature was counted to estimate its age?
explanation_en: Seasonal shell bands function like tree rings.

clue_en: Strawberry — What are the seed-like structures on a strawberry’s surface?
explanation_en: Each achene is a dry fruit containing one seed.

clue_en: Capsaicin — What is capsaicin’s molecular formula?
explanation_en: Capsaicin contains carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen.

clue_en: Western lowland gorilla — In which African region does the western lowland gorilla live?
explanation_en: Populations inhabit lowland forests of west-central Africa.

clue_en: Ming (clam) — What species was Ming?
explanation_en: Arctica islandica is the bivalve species commonly called the ocean quahog.

clue_en: Strawberry — To which plant family do strawberries belong?
explanation_en: Fragaria is in Rosaceae.

clue_en: Capsaicin — In which pepper tissue is capsaicin concentrated?
explanation_en: It is produced around the internal ribs, not mainly in seeds.

clue_en: Wöhler synthesis — Which doctrine claimed organic substances required a living vital force?
explanation_en: The synthesis weakened a strict divide between organic and inorganic chemistry.

clue_en: Ming (clam) — In 2013, what age was reported for the bivalve nicknamed Ming?
explanation_en: The revised estimate increased Ming’s reported age to 507 years.

clue_en: Strawberry — What word describes a fruit formed from many ovaries of one flower?
explanation_en: Each ovary contributes a small fruitlet.

clue_en: Capsaicin — Which heat-sensing receptor does capsaicin activate?
explanation_en: TRPV1 activation opens a cation channel and produces a heat sensation without itself increasing tissue temperature.

clue_en: Wöhler synthesis — Which inorganic salt rearranged to form urea?
explanation_en: The inorganic salt rearranges without changing its elemental formula, yielding an organic compound with a different structure.

clue_en: Uranium-238 — About how long is uranium-238’s half-life?
explanation_en: Its half-life is approximately 4.468 billion years.

clue_en: Strawberry — Botanically, is a strawberry a true berry?
explanation_en: It is an aggregate accessory fruit.

clue_en: Capsaicin — Which scale compares chilli-pepper pungency?
explanation_en: The Scoville scale expresses perceived pungency associated with capsaicinoid concentration.

clue_en: Wöhler synthesis — In what year was the Wöhler synthesis first reported?
explanation_en: The 1828 result became a landmark because it produced an organic compound from inorganic starting material.

clue_en: Uranium-238 — At the end of its decay series, uranium-238 becomes which stable element?
explanation_en: The uranium series terminates at lead-206.

clue_en: Star — What balance keeps a stable star from collapsing or exploding?
explanation_en: Outward pressure balances inward gravity.

clue_en: Capsaicin — Plants of which genus produce capsaicin?
explanation_en: Capsicum includes the chilli-pepper species that synthesize capsaicinoids in their fruits.

clue_en: Wöhler synthesis — Which German chemist performed the synthesis?
explanation_en: The experiment took the chemist’s name and became a landmark example in organic chemistry.

clue_en: Uranium-238 — What does the mass number in the isotope notation U-238 count?
explanation_en: An isotope’s mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons.

clue_en: Star — What process powers main-sequence stars?
explanation_en: Hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium, releasing energy.

clue_en: Coeliac disease — Which ancient physician gave an early description of the condition?
explanation_en: Aretaeus described an abdominal wasting illness in antiquity.

clue_en: List of chemical elements named after people — Which person has no officially named chemical element: Albert Einstein, Marie Curie, or Isaac Newton?
explanation_en: The people-namesake table includes Einstein and the Curies but has no Newton entry.

clue_en: Light-year — How many days does the fixed Julian year contain?
explanation_en: Astronomers use this fixed interval instead of a calendar year whose length varies with leap days.

clue_en: Pancreas — The pancreas lies mostly behind which organ?
explanation_en: It extends across the upper abdomen behind the stomach.

clue_en: Patella — Is the patella fully ossified at birth?
explanation_en: It begins largely as cartilage and ossifies during childhood.

clue_en: Human skeleton — How many bones form the appendicular skeleton?
explanation_en: Limbs and girdles make up the appendicular skeleton.

clue_en: Light-year — What abbreviation is commonly used for light-year?
explanation_en: The abbreviation comes from the initial letters of light and year and is used for interstellar distances.

clue_en: Pancreas — Is the pancreas both endocrine and exocrine?
explanation_en: It releases hormones into blood and digestive enzymes into ducts.

clue_en: Patella — Within which muscle group’s tendon is the patella embedded?
explanation_en: The patella is a sesamoid bone that develops inside this tendon and improves the knee extensor’s leverage.

clue_en: Human skeleton — How many bones form the axial skeleton?
explanation_en: The axial skeleton includes skull, vertebral column, and thoracic cage.

clue_en: Navel — The umbilicus typically lies near the junction of which two vertebral levels?
explanation_en: The umbilicus usually lies near the junction between the L3 and L4 vertebral levels.

clue_en: Pancreas — Which organ produces insulin?
explanation_en: This organ has endocrine islets that release hormones into the bloodstream.

clue_en: Patella — What type of bone is the patella?
explanation_en: It develops within a tendon.

clue_en: Human skeleton — Which skeletal division contains the limbs and their girdles?
explanation_en: The appendicular skeleton comprises the limbs plus shoulder and pelvic girdles.

clue_en: Navel — Which thoracic spinal nerve supplies skin at the level of the umbilicus?
accepted_variants_en: tenth thoracic spinal nerve|thoracic nerve T10
explanation_en: Skin around the waist at umbilical level is supplied by the T10 dermatome.

clue_en: Arm — Which Latin term serves as a root for many anatomical names of the arm?
explanation_en: Brachium can denote the arm as a whole or its upper part and supplies the root of many anatomical terms.

clue_en: Patella — What is the anatomical name for the kneecap?
explanation_en: The patella sits at the front of the knee.

clue_en: Human skeleton — What two divisions make up the human skeleton?
explanation_en: The adult skeleton is divided into axial and appendicular parts.

clue_en: Navel — Which three broad surface forms can a navel have?
accepted_variants_en: hollowed, flat, or protruding|protruding flat or hollowed
explanation_en: The detached scar can heal into protruding, flat, or hollowed forms.

clue_en: Arm — What joint joins the head of the humerus to the scapula?
explanation_en: The ball-like humeral head meets the scapula at this shoulder articulation.

clue_en: Lung — What double-layered membrane surrounds each lung?
explanation_en: Visceral and parietal pleura enclose a lubricated space.

clue_en: Human skeleton — How many bones are normally counted in an adult human skeleton?
explanation_en: Some individual variation occurs through fused or accessory bones.

clue_en: Navel — The navel marks the former attachment site of which fetal structure?
explanation_en: After the umbilical cord detaches, it leaves the scarred area called the navel.

clue_en: Arm — What is the arm region between the elbow and wrist called?
explanation_en: The forearm is the upper-limb region extending from the elbow to the wrist.

clue_en: Lung — Which fissure separates the right upper and middle lobes?
explanation_en: The oblique fissure separates the lower lobe.

clue_en: Capillary — Who received the 1920 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work on capillary function?
explanation_en: His research explained how capillaries provide nutrients to animal tissue.

clue_en: Navel — What anatomical word is another name for the navel?
explanation_en: The umbilicus is the central abdominal scar commonly called the navel or belly button.

clue_en: Arm — Which bone is not among the arm’s three named long bones: ulna, humerus, or tibia?
explanation_en: The source identifies humerus, ulna, and radius as the arm’s three long bones, excluding tibia.

clue_en: Lung — What tiny air sacs exchange gases with blood?
explanation_en: Thin alveolar walls permit diffusion.

clue_en: Capillary — Which 13th-century physician left the earliest known manuscript description of capillary passages?
explanation_en: He described perceptible passages between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein.

clue_en: Willem Einthoven — Which five letters label the standard successive electrocardiogram deflections?
response_en: P, Q, R, S and T
explanation_en: The conventional sequence runs from the atrial P wave through the ventricular T wave.

clue_en: Arm — What single long bone forms the upper arm?
explanation_en: This bone spans the shoulder to the elbow and is the sole long bone of the upper arm.

clue_en: Lung — How many lobes does the left lung have?
explanation_en: The left lung leaves space for the heart.

clue_en: Capillary — Who wrote in 1653 that blood passes from arteries into veins through connections or tissue porosities?
explanation_en: He inferred a route between the two vessel systems without directly seeing capillaries.

clue_en: Willem Einthoven — Which Dutch physiologist invented the first practical electrocardiograph and received the 1924 medicine Nobel?
explanation_en: His string-galvanometer system made clinical recording of the heart’s electrical activity practical.

clue_en: Pulmonary circulation — Who published De re anatomica in 1559 with an accurate description of blood passing through the lungs?
explanation_en: His account traced blood from the right side of the heart through the lungs to the left side.

clue_en: Lung — How many lobes does the right human lung have?
explanation_en: They are superior, middle, and inferior lobes.

clue_en: Capillary — Who first directly observed and correctly described capillaries in a frog's lung in 1661?
explanation_en: His microscopic observation supplied the missing link between arteries and veins.

clue_en: Christiaan Barnard — Who performed the first human-to-human heart transplant on 3 December 1967?
explanation_en: The operation took place at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.

clue_en: Pulmonary circulation — Which Spanish physician published an accurate European description of the lung blood-flow system in 1553?
explanation_en: The description appeared in his theological work Christianismi Restitutio.

clue_en: Gray's Anatomy — Who supplied the illustrations for the 1858 textbook Anatomy: Descriptive and Surgical?
explanation_en: His detailed anatomical plates accompanied the book’s first edition.

clue_en: Capillary — What are the smallest blood vessels?
explanation_en: Their microscopic diameter and thin walls place blood close to surrounding tissues.

clue_en: Stethoscope — Which French physician invented the stethoscope in 1816?
explanation_en: His original instrument was a monaural wooden tube used for listening to internal sounds.

clue_en: Pulmonary circulation — Which Renaissance polymath proposed that the heart was a muscle but still defended pores between the ventricles?
explanation_en: He moved toward a muscular view of the heart while retaining part of Galen’s model.

clue_en: History of anatomy — Which anatomist published De humani corporis fabrica in 1543, challenging animal-based teachings that had dominated European anatomy?
explanation_en: His treatise used detailed human dissection and illustrations to correct inherited anatomical claims.

clue_en: History of computed tomography — At which London hospital was the first clinical CT patient examined on 1 October 1971?
explanation_en: The first patient scan there was performed with neuroradiologist James Ambrose.

explanation_en: Two atria receive blood and two ventricles pump it.

clue_en: Pulmonary circulation — Which Greek physician first described the lung blood-flow system as distinct from circulation through the rest of the body?
explanation_en: His account treated the lung circuit separately, although many details remained inaccurate.

clue_en: Gray's Anatomy — Who wrote the anatomy textbook first published in London in 1858 as Anatomy: Descriptive and Surgical?
explanation_en: The reference work became commonly known as Gray's Anatomy.

clue_en: History of computed tomography — Which physicist shared the 1979 medicine Nobel for the development of computed tomography?
explanation_en: His mathematical reconstruction work complemented the engineering of clinical CT scanners.

clue_en: Frank Jobe — Which Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame pitcher underwent ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction in 1982?
explanation_en: His operation was the first performance of the procedure in Japan.

clue_en: Pulmonary artery — Which artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart?
explanation_en: Unlike most arteries, this vessel carries low-oxygen blood from the heart toward the lungs.

clue_en: History of anatomy — Which ancient physician’s animal-based anatomical teachings dominated Europe before the Renaissance?
explanation_en: Later human dissection exposed differences between Galen’s descriptions and human bodies.

clue_en: History of computed tomography — Which engineer developed the scanner used for the first clinical CT examination?
explanation_en: His system reconstructed cross-sectional images from X-ray measurements taken around the head.

clue_en: Tennis elbow — Which German physician is credited with the first 1873 description of the overuse condition later associated with racket sports?
explanation_en: He called the condition writer’s cramp, or Schreibekrampf.

clue_en: Quercus robur — What rounded structures occur at the bases of Quercus robur leaves?
explanation_en: Small lobes clasp the short petiole.

clue_en: Trapezius — Which major superficial muscle spans the neck and upper back?
explanation_en: The broad paired muscle spans the neck, shoulders, and upper back.

clue_en: Magnetic resonance imaging — Who used a magnetic-field gradient in 1973 to make a two-dimensional NMR image of two water tubes?
explanation_en: He called the method zeugmatography and imaged proton spin density in the two-tube sample.

clue_en: Frank Jobe — Which surgeon performed the first reconstruction of an ulnar collateral ligament on 25 September 1974?
explanation_en: He devised the operation for pitcher Tommy John, whose name later became attached to the procedure.

clue_en: Quercus robur — What common oak name refers to its long fruit stalks?
explanation_en: Its acorns hang on peduncles.

clue_en: Chlorophyll — Which metal ion lies at the centre of a chlorophyll molecule?
explanation_en: Magnesium is coordinated within the porphyrin-like ring.

clue_en: Tibia — The tibia is found in which part of the body?
explanation_en: The tibia runs from the knee to the ankle in the lower limb.

clue_en: Tennis elbow — What clinical term names the common racket-sport overuse condition affecting the common extensor tendon near the lateral epicondyle?
explanation_en: The condition involves pain associated with the common extensor origin near the lateral epicondyle.

clue_en: Quercus robur — How many rounded lobes usually occur on each side of a Quercus robur leaf?
explanation_en: Its leaves have three to six rounded lobes on each side, divided no farther than halfway to the midrib.

explanation_en: Weak green absorption produces the familiar appearance.

explanation_en: The native distribution spans most of Europe and continues east into western Asia.

explanation_en: Multiplying 365.25 days by 86,400 seconds gives 31,557,600 seconds.

explanation_en: Quercus robur is a large deciduous tree, not a shrub or herb.

explanation_en: Within chloroplasts, chlorophyll is concentrated in thylakoid membranes that capture light energy.

explanation_en: Curium, element 96, commemorates both Curies.

explanation_en: A parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends one arcsecond, equal to about 3.26 light-years.

clue_en: Pancreas — Into which part of the small intestine does the pancreatic duct empty?
explanation_en: Pancreatic juice enters near the start of the small intestine.

explanation_en: Chlorophyll reflects more green light than red or blue.

explanation_en: Mendelevium is listed as element 101 with the symbol Md.

explanation_en: Light travels about 9.46 × 10¹² km in one Julian year.

explanation_en: These islet cells release insulin in response to rising blood glucose.

explanation_en: It holds the tendon farther from the joint axis.
